candidate_relations.label: Brain metastasis of breast cancer
candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the CNS (primary CNS lymphoma), a distinct hematologic malignancy. While brain metastasis from HER2+ breast cancer is a common and clinically compelling differential in this context, the reference specifies a lymphomatous etiology rather than metastatic carcinoma. The two entities differ in cell lineage, treatment, and prognosis, making this an incompatible subtype/etiology rather than a partial or equivalent match.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Brain metastasis from breast cancer is a plausible differential but is a different diagnostic entity from primary CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of primary CNS DLBCL is unexpected given the strong clinical context of stage IV HER2+ breast cancer with prior systemic disease; the case may represent an incidental or treatment-related secondary malignancy, but the record does not provide histopathologic confirmation of the brain lesion to distinguish metastasis from lymphoma — this ambiguity is inherent to the case design.
